records.source: Worker sweeps can destroy unrelated Qt widgets on the wrong thread. A running GUI therefore services worker requests through :func:`spacr.qt.gc_policy.collect_once`. Repeated requests coalesce. Headless processes and the GUI thread retain synchronous collection; checking for an application does not import Qt into headless jobs.

An executing GUI therefore services worker requests through :func:`spacr.qt.gc_policy.collect_once`. Repeated requests coalesce. Headless processes and the main GUI execution path retain synchronous collection; checking for an application does not import Qt into headless jobs.

records.label: spacr.accelerator.cellpose_gpu#1
records.source: Cellpose does its own device resolution and already knows about MPS -- ``assign_device(gpu=True)`` answers ``mps`` on a Metal machine. What it cannot do is guess, so it must be TOLD there is a GPU. Passing ``torch.cuda.is_available()`` here pins a Mac to the CPU when no explicit device is supplied. An explicit Cellpose device takes precedence.
records.context: Cellpose does its own device resolution and already knows about MPS -- ``assign_device(gpu=True)`` answers ``mps`` on a Metal machine. What it cannot do is guess, so it must be TOLD there is a GPU. Passing ``torch.cuda.is_available()`` here pins a Mac to the CPU when no explicit device is supplied. An explicit Cellpose device takes precedence.
records.translation: Cellpose sér sjálft um val á tæki og þekkir nú þegar MPS -- ``assign_device(gpu=True)`` skilar ``mps`` á Metal-vél. Það sem það getur ekki er að giska, svo því verður að vera SAGT að til sé GPU. Að senda ``torch.cuda.is_available()`` hér festir Mac við CPU þegar ekkert tæki er sérstaklega tilgreint. Sérstaklega tilgreint Cellpose-tæki hefur forgang.
records.review_basis: written from the English (no current MT draft)

records.label: spacr.accelerator.cellpose_kwargs#4
records.source: ``use_bfloat16`` -- cpsam loads its weights in bfloat16 by default and Metal on torch 2.2 has no bfloat16, so the default is a ``TypeError: BFloat16 is not supported on MPS`` at construction. Measured on the reporting iMac; float32 weights work there and cost VRAM, which is the right trade for a card that otherwise sits idle. CPU inference also uses float32: bfloat16 support does not imply native arithmetic, and emulation can be substantially slower. This matches Make Masks; float32 arithmetic need not produce identical predictions to bfloat16.
records.context: ``use_bfloat16`` -- cpsam loads its weights in bfloat16 by default and Metal on torch 2.2 has no bfloat16, so the default is a ``TypeError: BFloat16 is not supported on MPS`` at construction. Measured on the reporting iMac; float32 weights work there and cost VRAM, which is the right trade for a card that otherwise sits idle. CPU inference also uses float32: bfloat16 support does not imply native arithmetic, and emulation can be substantially slower. This matches Make Masks; float32 arithmetic need not produce identical predictions to bfloat16.
records.translation: ``use_bfloat16`` -- cpsam hleður vigtum sínum sjálfgefið í bfloat16 og Metal á torch 2.2 hefur ekkert bfloat16, svo sjálfgefið leiðir til ``TypeError: BFloat16 is not supported on MPS`` við smíði. Mælt á iMac-tölvunni sem tilkynnti villuna; float32-vigtir virka þar og kosta VRAM, sem er rétt málamiðlun fyrir skjákort sem annars stendur aðgerðalaust. Ályktun á CPU notar líka float32: stuðningur við bfloat16 þýðir ekki innbyggða reikninga, og hermun getur verið talsvert hægari. Þetta samsvarar Make Masks; reikningar í float32 þurfa ekki að gefa sömu spár og bfloat16.
records.review_basis: written from the English (no current MT draft)

records.label: spacr.active_learning.retrain_round#26
records.source: ``{crop key: rejected class}`` -- suggestions the annotator REJECTED (:func:`spacr.suggest.rejected_suggestions`). In a two-class column a rejection of class 1 is an example of class 2, and it is fitted as one; a crop that has since been labelled is left to its label, and in a column with any other classes the rejection cannot be turned into a label and is counted in the notes instead. A rejection is information, not silence: without this the model that proposed the wrong class would be fitted on exactly the same evidence next round and propose it again.

records.label: spacr.cli_download#2
records.source: WHAT IT WILL AND WILL NOT DO WITHOUT BEING ASKED. With no arguments it fetches the example sets -- Import, Mask, Measure, Annotate/Classify, Replication, Recruitment and the synthetic Invasion set -- which come to about 1.8 GB. The OPS and Align & Stitch samples are fetched only when named (``spacr-download ops stitch``) or with ``all``. It does NOT fetch the published TSG101 screen, which is 33 GB. A command that spent 33 GB of somebody's quota because they typed its name with no arguments would be a bug however well documented, so the screen is opt-in, is asked for in pieces, and is confirmed before it starts. The pieces are :mod:`spacr.screen_data`'s, unchanged: four measurement databases of about 0.5 GB and four crop folders of about 8 GB, any subset of which can be named.

records.label: spacr.crop_loader#1
records.source: **WHAT IT IS FOR.** Every screen that shows objects has had its own way of finding them, and the Embeddings screen had none at all -- :meth:`spacr.qt.screens.embeddings.EmbeddingsScreen.set_crops` existed and nothing in ``spacr/`` called it, so the only route to a label-free vector was to open Python. This module is the missing half: it turns a question about a plate into a stack of pixels, and it does it in two steps so a GUI can stay answerable between them.
records.context: **What it is for.** Every application view that shows objects has had its own way of finding them, and the Embeddings application view had none at all -- :meth:`spacr.qt.screens.embeddings.EmbeddingsScreen.set_crops` existed and nothing in ``spacr/`` called it, so the only route to a label-free vector was to open Python. This module is the missing half: it turns a question about a plate into a stack of pixels, and it does it in two steps so a GUI can stay answerable between them.
records.translation: **TIL HVERS ÞAÐ ER.** Hver skjámynd sem sýnir hluti hefur haft sína eigin leið til að finna þá, og Embeddings-skjámyndin hafði enga -- :meth:`spacr.qt.screens.embeddings.EmbeddingsScreen.set_crops` var til en ekkert í ``spacr/`` kallaði á það, svo eina leiðin að merkjalausum vigri var að opna Python. Þessi eining er helmingurinn sem vantaði: hún breytir spurningu um plötu í stafla af pixlum, og gerir það í tveimur skrefum svo GUI geti áfram svarað á milli þeirra.
records.review_basis: written from the English (no current MT draft)

records.label: spacr.crop_loader#2
records.source: **PLANNING IS NOT LOADING, and that separation is the whole design.** :func:`plan_crops` asks the database or the folder *which objects match* and reads no pixels at all: a ``COUNT`` and a ``SELECT`` of identifiers, or one ``scandir``. It is milliseconds on a plate of sixty thousand crops, so a screen can run it on a click and tell the user what they asked for before committing to reading any of it. :func:`load_crops` then reads the pixels in pages, reporting after each one. A caller that runs the second half on a worker thread gets a progress number per page and a stop that takes effect within a page rather than at the end.
records.context: **Planning is not loading, and that separation is the whole design.** :func:`plan_crops` asks the database or the folder *which objects match* and reads no pixels at all: a ``COUNT`` and a ``SELECT`` of identifiers, or one ``scandir``. It is milliseconds on a plate of sixty thousand extracted image regions, so a screen can execute it on a click and tell the user what they asked for before committing to reading any of it. :func:`load_crops` then reads the pixels in pages, reporting after each one. A caller that executes the second half on a background execution unit gets a progress number per page and a stop that takes effect within a page rather than at the end.
records.translation: **ÁÆTLUN ER EKKI HLEÐSLA, og sá aðskilnaður er öll hönnunin.** :func:`plan_crops` spyr gagnagrunninn eða möppuna *hvaða hlutir passa* og les enga pixla: ``COUNT`` og ``SELECT`` á auðkennum, eða eitt ``scandir``. Það tekur millisekúndur á plötu með sextíu þúsund myndskurðum, svo skjámynd getur keyrt það við smell og sagt notandanum hvað hann bað um áður en hún skuldbindur sig til að lesa nokkuð af því. :func:`load_crops` les síðan pixlana í síðum og tilkynnir eftir hverja þeirra. Kallandi sem keyrir seinni helminginn á vinnsluþræði fær framvindutölu fyrir hverja síðu og stöðvun sem tekur gildi innan síðu frekar en í lokin.
records.review_basis: written from the English (no current MT draft)

records.label: spacr.crop_loader#3
records.source: **WHAT IT NEEDS.** Either a ``measurements.db`` -- where the crops are chosen by object class, by plate, or by a predicate over ``png_list`` -- or a folder of crop PNGs. Nothing else: the pixels themselves come from :func:`spacr.crops.resolve_crop_source`, so this module inherits the existing answer to "are there pre-generated crops here, or do we cut from ``merged/*.npy``" rather than inventing a second one, and a legacy folder is corrected on load exactly as it is everywhere else.
records.context: **What it needs.** Either a ``measurements.db`` -- where the extracted image regions are chosen by object class, by plate, or by a predicate over ``png_list`` -- or a folder of extracted image region PNGs. Nothing else: the pixels themselves come from :func:`spacr.crops.resolve_crop_source`, so this module inherits the existing answer to "are there pre-generated extracted image regions here, or do we cut from ``merged/*.npy``" rather than inventing a second one, and a legacy folder is corrected on load exactly as it is everywhere else.
records.translation: **HVAÐ ÞAÐ ÞARF.** Annaðhvort ``measurements.db`` -- þar sem myndskurðir eru valdir eftir hlutaflokki, eftir plötu eða eftir skilyrði yfir ``png_list`` -- eða möppu með myndskurðum í PNG. Ekkert annað: pixlarnir sjálfir koma frá :func:`spacr.crops.resolve_crop_source`, svo þessi eining erfir fyrirliggjandi svar við spurningunni „eru hér fyrirfram gerðir myndskurðir, eða skerum við úr ``merged/*.npy``“ frekar en að finna upp annað, og eldri mappa er leiðrétt við hleðslu nákvæmlega eins og alls staðar annars staðar.

records.label: spacr.crop_loader#6
records.source: **A CAP IS PART OF THE ANSWER, NOT A FAILURE TO LOAD EVERYTHING.** Sixty thousand crops of 96x96x3 is 1.6 GB before a backbone has seen one of them, and a screen that tries it dies on a machine that could have embedded the first two thousand happily. So :attr:`CropQuery.limit` is a real default and the plan says what it left behind -- "the first 2,000 of 61,433" -- rather than quietly returning a subset that looks like the whole plate.
records.context: **A cap is part of the answer, not a failure to load everything.** Sixty thousand extracted image regions of 96x96x3 is 1.6 GB before a backbone has seen one of them, and a screen that tries it dies on a machine that could have embedded the first two thousand happily. So :attr:`CropQuery.limit` is a real default and the plan says what it left behind -- "the first 2,000 of 61,433" -- rather than quietly returning a subset that looks like the whole plate.
records.translation: **HÁMARK ER HLUTI AF SVARINU, EKKI MISTÖK VIÐ AÐ HLAÐA ÖLLU.** Sextíu þúsund myndskurðir af stærð 96x96x3 eru 1.6 GB áður en grunnnet hefur séð einn þeirra, og skjámynd sem reynir það deyr á vél sem hefði vel getað fellt inn fyrstu tvö þúsund. Því er :attr:`CropQuery.limit` raunverulegt sjálfgefið gildi og áætlunin segir hvað hún skildi eftir -- „fyrstu 2,000 af 61,433“ -- frekar en að skila hljóðlega hlutmengi sem lítur út eins og öll platan.

records.label: spacr.crop_loader#7
records.source: **AND A CAP IS NOT THE ONLY THING THAT REMOVES A ROW, SO IT IS COUNTED ON ITS OWN.** The merged route drops every row it cannot cut, and reporting that as a cap is the same sentence read backwards: a complete answer dressed as a subset, telling the user to raise a limit that never bit. So :attr:`CropPlan.matched`, :attr:`CropPlan.selected` and :attr:`CropPlan.count` are three numbers, :attr:`CropPlan.capped` is the gap between the first two and :attr:`CropPlan.dropped` the gap between the last two, and they reach the panel as separate clauses.

records.label: spacr.diameter#6
records.source: 1. **Flatten.** Denoise with a 1 px Gaussian, then subtract a heavily smoothed copy (sigma = max(32, min(H, W) / 4)) to remove illumination gradients. The sigma is deliberately far larger than any plausible object so that flattening removes vignetting without eating the objects — the opposite trade-off (a tight rolling ball) shrinks what it is trying to measure. 2. **Reject noise.** Compare the structural amplitude of the flattened plane (p99 - p30) against the *pixel-level* noise scale, measured as ``1.4826 * MAD(img - gaussian(img, 1))`` on the raw plane. A pure-noise plane scores below 1; a plane with real objects scores in the tens. Below ``min_snr`` the field is discarded rather than thresholded, because Otsu will happily bisect pure noise and hand back a confident-looking number. 3. **Threshold and label.** Otsu, fill holes, label, drop components that touch the image border (truncated, so their size is a lie) and components that are absurd (equivalent diameter below ``min_object_diameter``, or area above ``max_object_fraction`` of the field). Sizes are equivalent diameters, ``2 * sqrt(area / pi)``. 4. **Drop specks, then take the median.** A textured or punctate stain (a mitochondrial cell stain, a parasite marker) thresholds into a few whole objects plus hundreds of 4-10 px specks, and a plain median counts every speck as an object: on spaCR's own test plate that put the cell at 8 px and the pathogen at 11 px against 175 px and 32 px in the curated masks, while the nucleus, whose stain is solid, came out right at 91 px. So the typical object is first located by the stained area it carries (the area-weighted median, which specks cannot move because they hold almost no area), everything narrower than :data:`SPECK_FRACTION` of it is dropped, and the characteristic size is the median of what remains. Small components that together hold :data:`SPECK_MAX_AREA_SHARE` of the stained area or more are a second population, not specks, and stay. 5. **Cross-check by distance transform.** Step 3 has one dominant failure mode: a confluent monolayer fuses into a single component, that component touches the border and is dropped, and the estimate is then computed from whatever debris survived — biased **low**, and silently. So the Euclidean distance transform of the (unfilled) foreground is computed as well, its local maxima are taken as one seed per object (two passes: a coarse pass sets the suppression radius for the refined pass), and a watershed on ``-EDT`` splits the fused foreground back into objects whose equivalent diameters are measured the same way.

A pure-noise plane scores below 1; a plane with real objects scores in the tens. Below ``min_snr`` the field is discarded rather than thresholded, because Otsu will happily bisect pure noise and hand back a confident-looking number. 3. **Threshold and label.** Otsu, fill holes, label, drop components that touch the image border (truncated, so their size is a lie) and components that are absurd (equivalent diameter below ``min_object_diameter``, or area above ``max_object_fraction`` of the field). Sizes are equivalent diameters, ``2 * sqrt(area / pi)``. 4. **Drop specks, then take the median.** A textured or punctate stain (a mitochondrial cell stain, a parasite marker) thresholds into a few whole objects plus hundreds of 4-10 px specks, and a plain median counts every speck as an object: on spaCR's own test laboratory microplate that put the cell at 8 px and the pathogen at 11 px against 175 px and 32 px in the curated masks, while the nucleus, whose stain is solid, came out right at 91 px. Small components that together hold :data:`SPECK_MAX_AREA_SHARE` of the stained area or more are a second population, not specks, and stay. 5. **Cross-check by distance transform.** Step 3 has one dominant failure mode: a confluent monolayer fuses into a single component, that component touches the border and is dropped, and the estimate is then computed from whatever debris survived — biased **low**, and silently. records.translation: 1. **Fletja út.** Afsuða með 1 px Gauss-síu og draga síðan frá mjög mýkt afrit (sigma = max(32, min(H, W) / 4)) til að fjarlægja lýsingarhalla. Sigma er viljandi miklu stærra en nokkur hugsanlegur hlutur svo að útflatningin fjarlægi skyggingu í jöðrum án þess að éta hlutina — öfug málamiðlun (þröng rúllandi kúla) minnkar það sem hún reynir að mæla. 2. **Hafna suði.** Bera byggingarsveifluvídd útflatta lagsins (p99 - p30) saman við suðkvarðann *á pixlastigi*, mældan sem ``1.4826 * MAD(img - gaussian(img, 1))`` á hráa laginu. Lag með eintómu suði fær minna en 1; lag með raunverulegum hlutum fær tugi. Undir ``min_snr`` er sjónsviðinu hent frekar en það þröskuldað, því Otsu tvískiptir fúslega eintómu suði og skilar tölu sem virðist örugg. 3. **Þröskulda og merkja.** Otsu, fylla göt, merkja, sleppa þáttum sem snerta jaðar myndarinnar (styttir, svo stærð þeirra er röng) og þáttum sem eru fráleitir (jafngilt þvermál undir ``min_object_diameter``, eða flatarmál yfir ``max_object_fraction`` af sjónsviðinu). Stærðir eru jafngild þvermál, ``2 * sqrt(area / pi)``. 4. **Sleppa ögnum og taka síðan miðgildið.** Áferðarmikil eða doppótt litun (hvatberalitun frumu, sníkjudýramerki) þröskuldast í fáeina heila hluti auk hundraða agna af stærð 4-10 px, og einfalt miðgildi telur hverja ögn sem hlut: á eigin prófunarplötu spaCR setti það frumuna í 8 px og sýkilinn í 11 px á móti 175 px og 32 px í yfirförnu grímunum, á meðan kjarninn, sem er litaður heill, kom rétt út í 91 px. Því er dæmigerði hluturinn fyrst staðsettur eftir lituðu flatarmálinu sem hann ber (flatarmálsvegna miðgildið, sem agnir geta ekki hreyft því þær hafa nánast ekkert flatarmál), öllu sem er mjórra en :data:`SPECK_FRACTION` af honum er sleppt, og einkennandi stærð er miðgildi þess sem eftir er. Litlir þættir sem saman hafa :data:`SPECK_MAX_AREA_SHARE` af lituðu flatarmálinu eða meira eru annað þýði, ekki agnir, og halda sér. 5. **Krossathuga með fjarlægðarvörpun.** Skref 3 hefur eina ríkjandi bilunarleið: samfellt einlag rennur saman í einn þátt, sá þáttur snertir jaðarinn og er sleppt, og matið er þá reiknað út frá því rusli sem lifði af — skekkt **niður á við**, og hljóðlaust. Því er evklíðska fjarlægðarvörpun forgrunnsins (ófyllts) einnig reiknuð, staðbundin hágildi hennar eru tekin sem eitt fræ fyrir hvern hlut (tvær umferðir: gróf umferð ákvarðar bælingarradíus fyrir fínni umferðina), og vatnaskil á ``-EDT`` skipta samrunna forgrunninum aftur í hluti þar sem jafngild þvermál eru mæld á sama hátt.

records.source: Running it again on a plate folder it has already processed resumes rather than starting over. Raw images an earlier run moved into ``orig/`` are read from there, and only the fields ``stack/`` lacks are built. Every ``stack/*.npy`` and ``masks/*.npz`` an earlier run left is checked before it is reused: a file cut short is renamed to ``<name>.damaged``, named in the log, and built again, a field stack from the raw images or channel folders and an archive from ``stack/``. A field stack with nothing left to build it from is recorded as a failure, so the run ends incomplete instead of quietly short of that field, and an archive with nothing left to build it from stops the run with an error that names it. When no field can be built at all, the error says what the folder does hold. In ``test_mode`` a plate whose raw images are gone is sampled from its ``stack/`` instead.
records.context: Executing it again on a laboratory microplate folder it has already processed resumes rather than starting over. Raw images an earlier run moved into ``orig/`` are read from there, and only the microscope fields of view ``stack/`` lacks are built. Every ``stack/*.npy`` and ``masks/*.npz`` an earlier run left is checked before it is reused: a file cut short is renamed to ``<name>.damaged``, named in the log, and built again, a microscope field of view stack from the raw images or image data channel folders and an archive from ``stack/``. A microscope field of view stack with nothing left to build it from is recorded as a failure, so the processing session ends incomplete instead of quietly short of that microscope field of view, and an archive with nothing left to build it from stops the processing session with an error that names it. When no microscope field of view can be built at all, the error says what the folder does hold. In ``test_mode`` a laboratory microplate whose raw images are gone is sampled from its ``stack/`` instead.
records.translation: Ef það er keyrt aftur á plötumöppu sem það hefur þegar unnið heldur það áfram frekar en að byrja upp á nýtt. Hráar myndir sem fyrri keyrsla færði í ``orig/`` eru lesnar þaðan, og aðeins sjónsviðin sem ``stack/`` vantar eru byggð. Hver ``stack/*.npy`` og ``masks/*.npz`` sem fyrri keyrsla skildi eftir er athuguð áður en hún er endurnýtt: skrá sem er stytt er endurnefnd í ``<name>.damaged``, nefnd í annálnum og byggð aftur, sjónsviðsstafli úr hráu myndunum eða rásamöppunum og skjalasafn úr ``stack/``. Sjónsviðsstafli sem ekkert er eftir til að byggja úr er skráður sem bilun, svo keyrslan endar ófullkomin í stað þess að vanta hljóðlaust það sjónsvið, og skjalasafn sem ekkert er eftir til að byggja úr stöðvar keyrsluna með villu sem nefnir það. Þegar ekki er hægt að byggja neitt sjónsvið segir villan hvað mappan raunverulega geymir. Í ``test_mode`` er í staðinn tekið sýni úr ``stack/`` plötu þar sem hráu myndirnar eru horfnar.

records.source: THE CHANNEL TOKEN IS RANKED, NOT READ AS A NUMBER, and that is the one decision here worth knowing about. ``C1``/``C2``/``C3`` and ``w1``/``w2`` and ``0``/``1``/``2`` all have to end up as channels 0, 1, 2, and there is no reading of ``C1`` that is right for all three -- a literal read makes the first set start at channel 1 and leaves channel 0 empty for ever. records.source: THE SET IS THE TABLE'S, NOT THE DROP'S. ``table`` remembers which token owns which column in :attr:`FieldTable.channel_tokens`, and a later drop is ranked against the union of what it brings and what is already there. Ranking each drop on its own instead would put a second field's ``C2`` in column 0 beside a first field's ``C1``, and the only sign of it would be in the database.

Ranking each drop on its own instead would put a second microscope field of view's ``C2`` in column 0 beside a first microscope field of view's ``C1``, and the only sign of it would be in the database.
records.translation: MENGIÐ TILHEYRIR TÖFLUNNI, EKKI SLEPPINGUNNI. ``table`` man hvaða tákn á hvaða dálk í :attr:`FieldTable.channel_tokens`, og síðari slepping er raðað miðað við sammengi þess sem hún kemur með og þess sem þegar er til staðar. Ef hverri sleppingu væri raðað sér myndi ``C2`` annars sjónsviðs lenda í dálki 0 við hliðina á ``C1`` fyrsta sjónsviðs, og eina merkið um það væri í gagnagrunninum.

records.source: The other way into this module. :func:`measure_crop` starts from a ``merged/`` folder a pipeline already built; this starts from a table a user filled in by dropping files onto it, writes that folder, and then calls :func:`measure_crop` ITSELF -- unchanged, with no flag saying where the fields came from. The database, the crops and the folder tree are therefore the Measure module's, because they are made by it.
records.context: The other way into this module. :func:`measure_crop` starts from a ``merged/`` folder a workflow already built; this starts from a table a user filled in by dropping files onto it, writes that folder, and then calls :func:`measure_crop` ITSELF -- unchanged, with no flag saying where the microscope fields of view came from. The database, the extracted image regions and the folder tree are therefore the Measure module's, because they are made by it.
records.translation: Hin leiðin inn í þessa einingu. :func:`measure_crop` byrjar á ``merged/`` möppu sem vinnsluferli hefur þegar byggt; þetta byrjar á töflu sem notandi fyllti út með því að sleppa skrám á hana, skrifar þá möppu og kallar síðan á :func:`measure_crop` SJÁLFT -- óbreytt, án flaggs sem segir hvaðan sjónsviðin komu. Gagnagrunnurinn, myndskurðirnir og möpputréð tilheyra því Measure-einingunni, því hún býr þau til.
